title: Floor 2: Nowhere zones
task:
Create trips_clean with every row of trips, plus three columns:
- pu_zone and do_zone: the zone name from zones (NULL when there is no match)
- zone_flag: the first label that applies, checking both pu_location_id and do_location_id:
  1. 'unmatched' if either id is NULL or not in zones
  2. 'unknown' if either id is 264
  3. 'outside_nyc' if either id is 265
  4. 'ok' otherwise
dirt:
SELECT row_id, pu_location_id, do_location_id FROM trips
WHERE pu_location_id IS NULL OR do_location_id IS NULL OR pu_location_id IN (264, 265) OR do_location_id IN (264, 265)
   OR pu_location_id NOT IN (SELECT location_id FROM zones) OR do_location_id NOT IN (SELECT location_id FROM zones)
guideTask: create trips_clean with every row of trips, plus three columns: pu_zone, do_zone and zone_flag.
card: Some trips start or end in a zone that is not on the map.
context: The depot needs to report where every trip started and ended, including trips whose locations cannot be matched. trips holds 7,171 trips with rerun copies already removed; zones is the location lookup. Keeping unmatched trips in the report prevents an incomplete picture of service and revenue.

refresher.title: Keep unmatched rows with LEFT JOIN
refresher.text: A JOIN matches keys between tables. A LEFT JOIN keeps every row on the left and puts NULL in the right columns when there is no match. Aliases such as r and z name the two table copies. Joining twice lets you look up two locations.
refresher.sql:
WITH rides(id, place) AS (VALUES (1, 10), (2, 99)),
places(id, name) AS (VALUES (10, 'Depot'))
SELECT r.id, z.name FROM rides r
LEFT JOIN places z ON z.id = r.place;

refresher.title: Label the first matching condition
refresher.text: CASE checks WHEN conditions in order and returns the first matching THEN value. ELSE handles the rest. Test missing values with IS NULL, not = NULL. OR means either condition can be true; IN checks membership in a list.
refresher.sql:
WITH places(id) AS (VALUES (10), (99), (NULL))
SELECT id, CASE WHEN id IS NULL THEN 'missing'
WHEN id IN (99) THEN 'outside' ELSE 'known' END AS flag
FROM places;

refresher.title: Save and count the joined result
refresher.text: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ... AS saves the query so you can rebuild it. COUNT(*) checks that a join kept the expected number of rows. GROUP BY makes one group per label; HAVING can filter those groups.

rulesText:
## Floor 2: Nowhere zones (joins, NULLs and sentinels)

- **Tables given:** `trips` (floor 1's reference output, 7,171 rows), `zones`.
- **The dirt:** real: 110 trips touch zone 264 "Unknown", 74 touch zone 265 "Outside of NYC".
  Planted: 15 drop-off ids are 0 (not in the lookup) and 10 drop-off ids are NULL.
- **Task:** create `trips_clean`: every row of `trips`, plus `pu_zone`, `do_zone` (the zone name,
  NULL when there is no match) and `zone_flag`, the first that applies:
  1. `'unmatched'`: either id is NULL or not in `zones`;
  2. `'unknown'`: either id is 264;
  3. `'outside_nyc'`: either id is 265;
  4. `'ok'`.
- **Expected:** 7,171 rows in and out. Flags: ok 6,962; unknown 110; outside_nyc 74; unmatched 25.
  An inner join to `zones` on both ids keeps only 7,146 rows (it silently loses 25).
- **Pass:** 7,171 rows; the multiset of `(row_id, pu_zone, do_zone, zone_flag)` equals the reference
  `data/reference/floor2.sql`; all columns of `trips` present and unchanged.
- **Aha line:** a join can drop rows without an error. "Unknown" (264) is in the lookup, so an anti-join cannot find it; a missing id (0, NULL) is not, so only a left join shows it. Flag, do not delete.
